purpose: Learner-facing Test V3 pathway map for foundations, departments, responsibility growth, context, and learning boundaries.
coreSkills: Safety awareness, stop-work judgment, and escalation
System reasoning: understanding how your task connects to the whole
Team coordination and professional crew conduct
Job readiness: preparation, reliability, and learning on the call

responsibilitySteps.title: Foundation
responsibilitySteps.description: Learn the language, workflow, communication habits, safety boundaries, and basic equipment awareness shared across live-event work.

responsibilitySteps.title: Assigned Work
responsibilitySteps.description: Complete defined tasks under direction, ask when uncertain, protect equipment and people, and hand work back cleanly.

responsibilitySteps.title: Department Technician
responsibilitySteps.description: Understand a department's workflow well enough to perform bounded technical work and recognize when to escalate.

responsibilitySteps.title: Specialist
responsibilitySteps.description: Build deeper system knowledge, troubleshooting judgment, documentation fluency, and advanced technical context.

responsibilitySteps.title: Lead / Supervisor
responsibilitySteps.description: Coordinate people, priorities, communication, handoffs, and work quality while keeping authority boundaries clear.

responsibilitySteps.title: Production Management
responsibilitySteps.description: Plan across departments using advances, schedules, labor coordination, documentation, budgets, change control, and closeout.

responsibilitySteps.title: Operational Leadership
responsibilitySteps.description: Think beyond one department or event and manage broader systems, standards, teams, and organizational outcomes.

contexts.title: Touring / Festival
contexts.description: Fast-moving outdoor and multi-stage environments where handoffs, weather awareness, logistics, and changing crews matter.

contexts.title: Arena / Stadium
contexts.description: Large crews, long travel paths, strict timing, shared infrastructure, and many simultaneous departments.

contexts.title: Theatre / Performing Arts
contexts.description: House systems, repertory workflow, cue discipline, scenic movement, and venue-specific practices.

contexts.title: Corporate / Convention
contexts.description: Client-facing work, breakout rooms, presentation systems, repeatable room standards, and rapid changeovers.

contexts.title: Broadcast / Sports
contexts.description: Camera, video, communications, timing, signal paths, and production roles that overlap with live-event systems.

contexts.title: Venue / House
contexts.description: Local systems knowledge, maintenance, recurring event workflows, and coordination with visiting productions.

contexts.title: Rental Shop / Warehouse
contexts.description: Prep, QC, inventory, receiving, repair escalation, labeling, packing, and truck-stage workflow.

contexts.title: Outdoor / Public Event
contexts.description: Temporary infrastructure, weather exposure, public interfaces, access planning, and changing site conditions.

contexts.title: Institutional / University / Civic
contexts.description: Production work inside organizations with their own procedures, staffing models, documentation, and approval chains.

pathways.title: General Production
pathways.eyebrow: Start here if you are new
pathways.summary: Build the shared habits that make every department easier to understand: crew workflow, communication, equipment handling, jobsite awareness, organization, and knowing when to ask.
outcomes: Communicate clearly with leads and crew
pathways.boundaryNote: Online learning prepares you to understand the work. Employers and designated leads still control task assignment and authorization on the jobsite.

pathways.title: Lighting
pathways.summary: Learn how a lighting department moves from preparation and load-in through system setup, control, show operation, troubleshooting, and load-out.
outcomes: See how technician work grows into lead responsibility
pathways.boundaryNote: Electrical, rigging, work-at-height, and other controlled tasks remain subject to qualified-person and employer authorization requirements.

pathways.title: Audio
pathways.summary: Build from audio support into signal-flow reasoning, communications, system awareness, troubleshooting, networking concepts, and deeper technical responsibility.
outcomes: Recognize common system roles and handoffs
Connect support work to advanced audio roles
pathways.coverageLabel: Strong course set; depth under owner review
pathways.boundaryNote: Course understanding does not replace equipment-specific training, system commissioning authority, or employer approval.

pathways.title: Video / LED / AV
pathways.summary: Learn how video, LED, playback, camera, data, and display systems connect, and how support work develops into deeper system responsibility.
outcomes: Recognize major video and LED system components
Follow signal and data paths conceptually
Connect field support to advanced video roles
pathways.coverageLabel: Broad course set; advanced breadth under owner review
pathways.boundaryNote: Structural support, rigging, production power, and other controlled work remain outside the authority granted by online course completion.

pathways.title: Staging / Scenic / Carpentry
pathways.summary: Learn staging and scenic workflow through component awareness, coordinated movement, documentation, handoffs, system context, and leadership responsibility.
outcomes: Recognize common staging and scenic components
Understand build and strike workflow conceptually
Protect components during movement and staging
See how support work develops into planning and lead roles
pathways.boundaryNote: Structural decisions, powered equipment, engineered systems, and other controlled tasks remain with appropriately designated personnel.

pathways.title: Shop / Warehouse / Logistics
pathways.summary: Learn the prep, QC, inventory, receiving, labeling, packing, truck-stage, repair-escalation, and logistics work that keeps productions moving before and after show day.
outcomes: Connect shop work to show-site readiness
pathways.boundaryNote: Powered equipment, driving, repair, charging, hazardous materials, and other controlled tasks require the training and authorization appropriate to that workplace.

pathways.title: Backline / Props / Wardrobe
pathways.summary: Understand three distinct support areas through item handling, department workflow, communication, documentation, status tracking, and clean handoffs.
outcomes: Handle assigned items with care and traceability
Use clear handoff and status communication
Understand how support roles deepen with experience
pathways.boundaryNote: Artist, instrument, costume, property, and production-specific procedures remain subject to the responsible department's instructions.

pathways.title: Crew Lead / Supervisor
pathways.summary: Shift from completing your own tasks to coordinating people, priorities, communication, handoffs, quality, and escalation without exceeding your decision authority.
outcomes: Give and receive clear work direction
Model safe escalation and stop-work judgment
Separate leadership from unauthorized technical decisions
pathways.boundaryNote: Leadership responsibility does not automatically create technical qualification. Leads still work within employer, venue, department, and legal authority boundaries.

pathways.title: Production Coordination / Management
pathways.summary: Learn how productions are advanced, documented, scheduled, coordinated, changed, tracked, and closed out across departments and stakeholders.
outcomes: Connect technical departments without replacing their authority
pathways.boundaryNote: Management learning explains coordination and decision systems; it does not make the learner the qualified authority for every technical department.

pathways.title: Rigging & Production Power Awareness
pathways.summary: Learn enough to recognize the interfaces, vocabulary, hazards, stop conditions, handoff points, and qualification boundaries around controlled specialty work.
outcomes: Recognize when a task enters a controlled specialty
Use correct escalation and handoff behavior
Understand that awareness is not qualification
Identify the designated authority before acting
pathways.boundaryNote: Crew Blueprint does not authorize rigging, energized electrical work, generator operation, work at height, rescue, or other qualified-person activities.
